latest_news.headline: North Korea revision: Japan reports 220 km and over 910 km flights; no EEZ entry confirmed
latest_news.text: Japan’s October 12 Ministry of Defense/Cabinet Secretariat publication was retrieved in full. It estimates at least two ballistic missiles fired from inland North Korea toward the northeast/east: around 09:19 JST, approximately 220 km range and 20 km maximum altitude; around 09:36 JST, more than 910 km range and approximately 70 km maximum altitude. The release says entry into Japanese territory or its EEZ has not been confirmed and no aircraft or vessel damage reports have been confirmed. Japan, the US and South Korea are analyzing details, including a possible irregular trajectory for the second missile. NHK repeats the minister’s same estimates and is not independent sensor verification. The PM’s primary instructions concern information gathering, aircraft/vessel safety and contingency readiness, not a new combat operation. This revises the retained same-launch account with primary operational estimates and corrects its earlier missing-original-source context; it is not a new launch during this scan. Publication dates are October 12 but exact publication instants remain unknown. Approximate launch times are official estimates, not independently established event instants. System identity, trajectory and motive remain independently unverified. Earlier versions are retained unchanged.
latest_news.originating_source: Japan Ministry of Defense and Cabinet Secretariat primary publication
latest_news.implication: Primary detail updates the already reported launch, not a new incident; flight estimates and possible irregular trajectory remain official assessments.
latest_news.next_trigger: Japan says US-Japan-South Korea analysis continues; no completion time or missile-system identification is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: Primary Japanese estimates add separate 220 km/20 km and >910 km/70 km flights; source gap corrected.

latest_news.headline: Pavlograd district: emergency service reports enterprise fire after overnight strike
latest_news.text: Ukraine’s State Emergency Service reports that an overnight Russian strike caused a large fire at an enterprise in Pavlograd district, Dnipropetrovsk region, and that rescuers extinguished it. The publication does not supply an exact strike time, enterprise identity, casualty count or independently established attribution. This is a new October 12 overnight episode, distinct from the October 11 warehouse fire in Samarivskyi district. The official account’s existence is verified; the operational claims are not independently verified.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukraine State Emergency Service official Telegram statement
latest_news.implication: An official account reports an extinguished industrial-site fire; damage, casualties and attribution are not independently established.
latest_news.next_trigger: No follow-up assessment or dated operational trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: North Korea: Seoul reports multiple ballistic launches; Japan reports two fallen projectiles
latest_news.text: Newly reviewed October 12 launch, occurring before this three-hour review window. Reuters reports South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff saying multiple ballistic missiles of apparently different types were fired near Pyongyang around 00:20 UTC; one type reportedly flew more than 900 km. Japan’s coast guard separately reported two projectiles believed to be ballistic missiles that had fallen. The Japan Times attributes two launch detections and splashdowns outside Japan’s exclusive economic zone to Japan’s Defense Ministry. South Korea’s National Security Office reportedly convened an emergency meeting and condemned the launches. Original JCS, Japanese coast-guard and ministry releases were not retrieved. These are attributed official sensor and political accounts, not independently authenticated trajectories or capability. Reuters syndication supplies no additional independent verification. The JCS characterizes the launches as a show of force after Seoul’s hypersonic test; that is not proven motive. Exact launch instants, weapons and independent operational corroboration remain unknown. Do not merge with the October 3 Wonsan event or call this a newly occurring strike in the scan window.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters original reporting; South Korean JCS and Japanese coast-guard attributed accounts
latest_news.implication: Officials report another North Korean missile test after Seoul’s hypersonic test; trajectories, capability and motive remain independently unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

latest_news.headline: Dammam airport: Reuters witness reports projectile impact; GACA is reported to assess damage
latest_news.text: Reuters reports a taxiing-aircraft witness saw a projectile hit tarmac near parked aircraft at about 17:30 UTC on October 11, causing fire; the aircraft returned to the gate and passengers were told to leave. Reuters and Anadolu report GACA confirming an attack on King Fahd International Airport and ongoing damage and safety assessments. Casualties, damage extent and current operating status are unknown. The GACA original statement was not retrieved. The Reuters witness adds firsthand reporting beyond the repeated official account, but no separate independent verification of the impact or Houthi attribution is established. Exact event and publication instants remain unknown; the witness time is approximate. This is distinct from Riyadh and from the earlier Dammam-vicinity projectile report on October 10.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters original eyewitness reporting, carried by Al-Monitor; Anadolu quoting GACA
latest_news.implication: Reuters reports disruption at a second Saudi airport; damage, casualties and current flight availability remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: GACA is reported to be conducting damage and safety inspections; no completion or reopening timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Riyadh Terminal 4: reports cite GACA on one killed and 11 injured after Sunday attack
latest_news.text: Reuters reports the Saudi-led coalition saying an unidentified projectile hit Terminal 4 on October 11 and caused a fire. A later Anadolu report dated October 12 and the updated DW body attribute one death and 11 injuries to GACA; the deceased is reported to be a Pakistani resident. Material damage is reported still being assessed. The primary GACA follow-up was not retrieved, and casualty counts, projectile identity and responsibility are not independently verified. This is a distinct October 11 episode, not a revision of the October 10 attack. Exact attack and publication instants are unknown; Anadolu metadata lacks a timezone. The obsolete DW URL headline implying 11 deaths is not used: the retrieved canonical body says one death and 11 injuries.
latest_news.originating_source: Anadolu and Reuters quoting GACA/coalition; DW with agency reporting
latest_news.implication: New attributed fatal casualties and terminal damage are reported at Riyadh; casualty totals and current operating status remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Damage assessments are reported ongoing; no completion or reopening timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Riyadh October 10 revision: Reuters reports Indian casualty death raises toll from 12 to 13
latest_news.text: Reuters reports that India’s embassy said on October 11 one Indian national injured in the October 10 Riyadh attack died, raising the previously reported 12-death toll to 13. DW relays the same embassy statement. This concerns the retained Saturday attack, not the separate Sunday Terminal 4 episode. The embassy original and independently counted casualty totals were not retrieved. The preceding report of 309 injured is retained as an earlier account, not recalculated or independently reaffirmed. All earlier versions remain unchanged.
latest_news.originating_source: Reuters and DW relaying Indian embassy statement
latest_news.implication: An attributed subsequent death revises the retained Saturday toll to 13; this is not another attack and totals remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No independent casualty-reconciliation or reopening timetable is supplied.
latest_news.material_revision: Reported subsequent death of an injured Indian national raises Saturday toll from 12 to 13.

latest_news.headline: CENTCOM says U.S. jet disabled cargo ship Ocean Molica in Gulf of Oman
latest_news.text: CENTCOM’s original October 10 public release says a U.S. fighter jet struck the stern of Panama-flagged Ocean Molica, also called Arika Sun, in the Gulf of Oman after repeated warnings, disabling propulsion without harming crew. It says the vessel had departed an Iranian port and attempted to violate the blockade. gCaptain repeats that statement and describes released military imagery; that is the same reporting chain, not independent verification of damage, crew condition or alleged blockade violation. Event date is October 10; exact strike and publication instants remain unknown. This newly reviewed older event is not represented as an attack within this three-hour window and is not linked to an unnamed UKMTO tanker incident.
latest_news.originating_source: U.S. Central Command original public release; gCaptain relaying CENTCOM
latest_news.implication: CENTCOM reports disabling a named commercial vessel during blockade enforcement; damage, crew condition and the alleged violation remain independently unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No follow-up or release timetable is supplied by the reviewed statement.

latest_news.headline: Pisochyn shop strike: police report three killed and 25 injured; emergency service says at least 22
latest_news.text: Police report three killed, including a 16-year-old boy, and 25 injured after an evening strike damaged a shop, apartment buildings and cars in Pisochyn. The emergency service separately reports three killed and at least 22 injured, including two children, and a 300-square-metre fire extinguished. Injury counts are not reconciled. Ukrainska Pravda reports a separate governor account of nine injured, not independent verification.
latest_news.originating_source: National Police of Ukraine; State Emergency Service of Ukraine
latest_news.implication: Official accounts report civilian deaths and damage at Pisochyn, distinct from the earlier Kharkiv residential strike; differing injury counts remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Police say a war-crime investigation has been opened; no findings timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Zelensky backs announced energy truce but reports later Kyiv and Kharkiv power strikes
latest_news.text: Zelensky’s public October 11 post supports the announced energy ceasefire while awaiting US details. A later public post says a drone struck a Kyiv power station with district outages, followed by strikes on energy facilities in Kharkiv region, after Trump’s announcement. AP reporting and the Guardian relay these statements; they do not independently verify the impacts. AP says Moscow did not immediately comment. The announcement is not an established implemented ceasefire, and Russian assent, attack timing and compliance remain unverified.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukrainian presidency official Telegram statement
latest_news.implication: The announced energy truce is not established as implemented: Kyiv reports later strikes, and Russian assent and compliance remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Kyiv explicitly awaits US details and reciprocal Russian support; no implementation deadline is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Kharkiv revision: emergency service reports fire extinguished and nine hurt; mayor account says ten
latest_news.text: A 15:59 UTC emergency-service follow-up reports the residential fire extinguished, one woman killed and nine people injured, including a seven-year-old boy. Its earlier statement reported eight injured. An earlier 12:17 UTC mayor post says ten injured and 35 houses and eight cars damaged. The counts are not reconciled and do not establish a later increase to ten.

latest_news.implication: The service reports the fire extinguished and nine injured; an earlier mayor account says ten. Casualty totals and responsibility remain independently unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.
latest_news.material_revision: Emergency service raises its injury count from eight to nine and reports fire extinguished; an earlier mayor account reports ten, unreconciled.

latest_news.implication: The service reports a cargo-terminal fire and temporary responder withdrawals; no injuries are reported, while responsibility and disruption remain unverified.

latest_news.headline: UKMTO 164-26: company reports tanker hit in Hormuz; crew reported safe
latest_news.text: UKMTO warning 164-26 reports an incident dated October 11 at 12:00 UTC in the Strait of Hormuz. A Company Security Officer reports that an outbound tanker was struck on the port side by an unidentified projectile, damaging the vessel. All crew are reported safe and no environmental impact was reported at the time. Vessel name, attacker and damage extent are not supplied. This is a new numbered reporting product, not independently confirmed evidence of a different hull or an extension of warning 162-26. No fire is reported in 164-26. The publication instant is unknown.
latest_news.originating_source: UK Maritime Trade Operations original warning 164-26, source Company Security Officer
latest_news.implication: The company reports tanker damage in Hormuz; crew are reported safe, but vessel identity, attacker and damage extent remain unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: UKMTO says authorities are investigating; no findings timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Kharkiv: emergency service reports one woman killed and eight hurt in residential strike
latest_news.text: Ukraine State Emergency Service post 77310, published at 13:58 UTC on October 11, reports a daytime Russian airstrike in the private residential sector of Kharkiv’s Nemyshlianskyi district. It reports a 36-year-old woman killed and eight people injured, including a child, a destroyed house, damage to neighboring homes and a 600-square-metre fire involving a residential building, cars and reeds. These are official attributed casualty, weapon and responsibility claims, not independently verified findings. The exact strike time is unknown. No connection to the retained October 10 medical-building strike or evacuation-vehicle incident is established.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukraine State Emergency Service original Telegram post 77310
latest_news.implication: The service reports civilian deaths, injuries and residential damage; casualty totals and responsibility remain independently unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia clarification: emergency-service spokesperson tells Ukrainska Pravda updated toll is 23
latest_news.text: Ukrainska Pravda reports directly contacting the President’s Office and the regional emergency service about the discrepancy between 20 and 23 fatalities. It quotes spokesperson Yuliia Barysheva saying the updated figure is 23. This clarifies an official account of the retained October 10 strike, not a new strike or independently verified death count.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukrainska Pravda; named regional State Emergency Service spokesperson
latest_news.implication: A named emergency-service spokesperson aligns the official toll with the president’s 23; the clarification remains an attributed account, not independent casualty verification.
latest_news.next_trigger: Public context unavailable; consult the original source.
latest_news.material_revision: Named emergency-service spokesperson explains updated official toll of 23 after earlier 20; no independent verification.

latest_news.headline: Sloviansk: emergency service reports seven wounded and five rescued after apartment strike
latest_news.text: Ukraine’s emergency service’s original October 11 post at 11:43:39 UTC reports seven people wounded in a Russian airstrike on apartment buildings in Sloviansk. It says five people were rescued: a man removed from rubble and transported to hospital, and four people evacuated using ladders. The service reports hits on nine- and five-storey buildings, nine damaged apartment buildings and a shop, and two apartment fires extinguished. Zelenskyy’s earlier original statement at 09:08:27 UTC describes a morning strike on a five-storey building in Sloviansk, a destroyed entrance section and possible people under rubble. These are related attributed official reports, not independent verification or proof of a broader escalation. Exact strike time and responsibility remain unverified; no death toll is supplied. This is distinct from the retained October 10 Kramatorsk nonresidential-fire report.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukraine State Emergency Service original statement
latest_news.implication: Emergency service reports civilian injuries and apartment damage, with five rescued and two fires extinguished; independent verification is absent.
latest_news.next_trigger: No further rescue-update timetable or evidence-backed operational trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia revision: president reports 23 dead; earlier governor account said 20
latest_news.text: Zelenskyy’s original October 11 statement at 09:08:27 UTC reports that morning search-and-rescue work ended in Zaporizhzhia and that 23 people died, including four children. It updates the same October 10 residential airattack previously reported by the governor at 07:19:07 UTC as 20 deaths, including four children, and 34 people seeking medical help. The governor’s earlier original post still says 20; his later 11:44:46 UTC post forwards the president’s 23-death statement rather than supplying an independent count. The emergency service also forwards the same presidential statement. The differences remain unreconciled; no independent casualty verification or precise revision/event time is established. Retain all earlier versions; this is not a new strike. The reviewed Ukrainska Pravda article still attributes 20 deaths to earlier official accounts.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy original statement
latest_news.implication: The president raises the reported death toll for the same October 10 strike; official counts remain unreconciled and independently unverified.
latest_news.next_trigger: No further casualty-update timetable or evidence-backed operational trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Kramatorsk: emergency service says repeat-attack threat forced rescue work to pause
latest_news.text: The emergency service's original October 11 post at 08:14:27 UTC describes a strike on a non-residential building during the preceding afternoon, October 10. It says a two-storey building and annex burned across 500 square metres. Rescuers contained the fire but had to suspend work because of the continuing threat of repeated attacks. The service also describes a contained fire in the private residential sector after an airstrike; linkage between these fires is not established. No casualty count, exact strike instant or resumption time is supplied. These are attributed official accounts, not independent attack verification. The report is not merged with the distinct October 8 passenger-bus attack.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukraine State Emergency Service original statement
latest_news.implication: Emergency service reports fire-response work suspended under repeat-attack threat; casualty count and resumption time are unknown.
latest_news.next_trigger: No resumption time or evidence-backed next trigger is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Zaporizhzhia revision: governor says rescue completed; 20 dead, including four children
latest_news.text: The governor's original October 11 statement at 07:19:07 UTC says search-and-rescue work for the October 10 city airattack is completed. It reports 20 deaths, including four children, and 34 people who sought medical help, with eight hospitalized. This revises the earlier governor account of 20 deaths and 32 injured and the earlier emergency-service account of three child deaths. The retained emergency-service post still reports 20 dead, three children among them, and 18 injured, with rescue continuing; its exact edit time is unknown. The current Ukrainska Pravda article reports 32 injured in its headline and added administration update while retaining the earlier SES quotation of 18; its edit instant is unknown. These are not independently authenticated casualty counts. Thirty-four people seeking medical help is not silently relabelled as 34 injured, and the separate regional 37-injury daily aggregate is not substituted for this city attack. Earlier versions remain retained; this is the same incident, not a new strike.
latest_news.originating_source: Zaporizhzhia governor Ivan Fedorov original statement
latest_news.implication: Governor reports completed rescue, a revised child-death count and ongoing treatment; casualty definitions and differing official accounts remain unreconciled.
latest_news.next_trigger: The governor says municipal cleanup and medical care continue; no further reporting timetable is supplied.

latest_news.headline: Dnipropetrovsk: emergency service reports six hurt, including two children and a rescuer
latest_news.text: Ukraine's emergency service says overnight and morning attacks affected four districts of Dnipropetrovsk region. It reports six people hurt: four in Dnipro including two children, a rescuer in Nikopol district and a man in Synelnykove district. It says 30 people, including a child, were rescued from a Dnipro building; apartment buildings, warehouses and a fire station were damaged. It also reports damage to a house and gas pipeline in Zelenodolsk community. All fires were extinguished according to the service. The original post is published October 11 at 07:04:29 UTC. Exact attack times, casualty totals and responsibility are attributed, not independently verified. This reporting period is not merged with the separate October 10 Nikopol child-death report.
latest_news.originating_source: Ukraine State Emergency Service original statement
latest_news.implication: Emergency service reports injuries and damage to homes, a fire station and a gas pipeline; all fires reportedly extinguished. Independent verification is absent.
latest_news.next_trigger: No further reporting timetable or evidence-backed next trigger is supplied.

source_limitations: Source coverage and corroboration have not been independently verified for this build. Official releases are preferred for attributable actions; reputable reporting may add context. Headline indexes, repeated reports and market prices are not independent confirmation. Missing or stale reports do not establish calm. Single-source claims remain unverified.
